Ellis — thanks, this is helpful. I pulled together a short playbook and a recommendation summary (attached). High-level guidance below; full notes and a quick action plan are attached as two files (architecture sketch + comparison CSV).

Summary recommendation (pilot):
- Start with a PrivateLink / interface endpoint for the production pilot. Reasoning: preserves strong tenancy isolation, simplifies firewalling, and minimizes PCI blast radius. PrivateLink gives you request-level endpoint control with AWS-managed endpoint ENIs in your VPC.

Tradeoffs:
- Latency: PrivateLink typically adds ~5–20ms depending on AZ topology vs peering. It usually meets your 150ms P95 requirement, but we should test with your real traffic shape.
- IP visibility: PrivateLink terminates on ENIs; source IP is NATed. If source-IP preservation is mandatory for your rate-limiting rules, peering keeps src IPs intact.
- Operational effort/cost: PrivateLink has per-hour endpoint and data processing costs but is lower engineering lift (no site-to-site tunnel management).

Fallback / resilience:
- Pair PrivateLink with a managed S2S VPN as a fallback route for cross-AZ failures or when you need full source-IP fidelity during a limited testing window.

Procurement items to expect for the pilot:
- Interface endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) costs + data transfer;
- Optional managed VPN appliance / Termination (if you choose IP preservation fallback);
- SOC2 artifact collection window (we will provide audit logs and connection diagrams).

Action items:
1) We will run a 48-hour latency & fidelity test from your staging VPC to a Redwood Private pilot endpoint (requires an interface endpoint and a small NAT/route change).
2) If you need source-IP preservation for production, we will present a peering plan with NATing constraints and route tables.
3) Procurement to approve interface endpoint + 1-month managed VPN standby.

I'll loop Neha for security compliance questions and Marcus for ops runbook input.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Ellis / team — quick operational notes from our side:

If you go PrivateLink for pilot:
- We recommend enabling cross-account VPC endpoint policies scoped to the minimal subnet/service principals; prevents broad access if route tables are misconfigured.
- For rate-limiting and audit logs, we will emit token-level traces in the Redwood Console and provide per-request metadata so you can enforce limits at the application layer (even if source-IP is NATed).
- Suggest a short-lived peering window during the pilot (48–72 hrs) to validate end-to-end source-IP behavior. Peering is a one-way peering (your VPC -> our service VPC) and we’ll provide a NAT design to avoid opening inbound surface area.

Operational checklist for procurement:
- Interface endpoint request + subnet/route configuration (estimated 2–4 hours eng time)
- Managed VPN standby with 1 static /24 for endpoint reachability (procurement for VPN appliance if you run on-prem)
- Security review slot (we need a 1-hour call with your InfoSec to sign off on endpoint policy)

If you strongly prefer source-IP preservation from day 1, peering is viable but:
- It increases surface area (you must lock down SGs, route tables and consider VPC sharing constraints).
- Cross-account peering requires tighter IAM & network ACL discipline.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Product Ops Manager, Redwood Inference

Ellis — a couple of hands-on performance notes from infra:

We ran throughput micro-benchmarks against a PrivateLink-backed test endpoint earlier this quarter. Observations:
- P50 latency delta vs VPC peering: ~8ms; P95 delta: ~12–18ms depending on pathing and whether traffic crosses AZ boundaries. Within your 150ms P95 budget this is fine for most model sizes.
- For high-concurrency workloads, PrivateLink's connection scaling is simpler (AWS handles the endpoint); peering requires you to size NAT & egress capacity if you rely on NAT.
- For strict source-IP logging: the only path that preserves original client IP end-to-end is peering or a direct on-prem interconnect (DX/DirectConnect). S2S VPN will also NAT unless you terminate in a way that preserves the IP (uncommon).

Operational recommendation:
- Pilot: PrivateLink + short peering window for source-IP validation.
- Production (if you need IP fidelity): Either permanent peering with strict route & SG policy, or a DirectConnect for guaranteed lower jitter (but higher procurement lead time).

Marcus Lin
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
